common.run-command.html: The command this control stands in for, copy-pasteable exactly as printed. It is shown on a refusal too, where it is the one remaining way to start what was just declined.

common.correlation-id.label: Correlation id
common.correlation-id.html: The id the service's own log lines for this request carry, worth quoting in a support message. It appears only where the response carried one, because an id matching no log line is a false lead.

common.error-copy-details.label: Copy details
common.error-copy-details.html: Puts the message, the remedy and the advanced detail on the clipboard as text, so none of it has to be retyped off the screen. Where the browser offers no clipboard at all, as on a plain unencrypted origin, it says so rather than appearing to have worked.

common.error-retry.label: Try again
common.error-retry.html: Repeats the request that failed, and changes nothing else. A service that is still down answers identically, which the line beside this records so the unchanged words are not mistaken for an unresponsive control.

common.error-retried-at.label: Retry result
common.error-retried-at.html: The clock time of the most recent attempt. It is on screen because an identical outcome otherwise looks like a control that did nothing at all.

wizard.command-echo.label: Equivalent command
wizard.command-echo.html: The command-line invocation this control is equivalent to, printed before the control is pressed. Copying or running the line is safe: no flag on this surface takes a secret, and reading it changes nothing.

wizard.configuration-saved.label: Configuration saved
wizard.configuration-saved.html: The configuration was written and is intact; only this running process could not begin serving it. Restarting the container or service picks it up, and none of it has to be entered again.

wizard.configure.mark-stale.label: Stale check
wizard.configure.mark-stale.html: A pass belongs to the values it was obtained for, so editing one drops it. Saving stays blocked until this destination has been tested again as it now stands.

wizard.configure.cancel.label: Cancel
wizard.configure.cancel.html: Closes these steps and writes nothing. The destination is left exactly as it stands, configured or not.

wizard.configure.next-test.label: Next: test connection
wizard.configure.next-test.html: Moves to the check step and starts the check straight away, using the values on this form. Nothing is saved by checking.

wizard.configure.back-fields.label: Back to the values
wizard.configure.back-fields.html: Returns to the form with every value kept. A pass already obtained still counts while nothing is edited, and stops counting the moment something is.

wizard.configure.retest.label: Test connection again
wizard.configure.retest.html: Writes a real object to this destination, reads it back and removes it. A refusal leaves the destination exactly as unproven as it is now.

wizard.configure.next-review.label: Next: review
wizard.configure.next-review.html: Moves to the last step, which shows what the save will write. Out of reach until a check has passed for the values on the form.

wizard.configure.back-test.label: Back to the check
wizard.configure.back-test.html: Returns to the check step without saving. The pass already recorded is kept.

wizard.configure.save.label: Save configuration
wizard.configure.save.html: Writes this destination in one request, after the check that proved it. A retention tier can select it from then on.

wizard.destination.step.label: Step position
wizard.destination.step.html: Which of the three steps is showing. Choosing a backend and naming the instance are separate because several destinations can be instances of one backend, and none of these steps writes anything.

wizard.destination.cancel.label: Cancel
wizard.destination.cancel.html: Abandons the new destination. Nothing has been written by this point, so nothing is left behind.

wizard.destination.next-name.label: Next: name this instance
wizard.destination.next-name.html: Carries the chosen backend to the naming step. Unavailable while the selected row is a backend this build describes and cannot yet store.

wizard.destination.back.label: Back
wizard.destination.back.html: Returns to the previous step with the answers already given kept. Still nothing is written.

wizard.destination.next-confirm.label: Next: confirm
wizard.destination.next-confirm.html: Moves to the summary of what will be created. Unavailable while the name is one the engine itself would refuse.

wizard.destination.existing-names.label: Names already taken
wizard.destination.existing-names.html: The instances of this backend that already exist. A destination name is unique, so these are the names this one cannot have.

wizard.destination.summary.label: What will be created
wizard.destination.summary.html: The backend and the name this destination will be declared with. Its own settings are not asked for here: the configure step collects them and performs the single write.

wizard.destination.next-configure.label: Next: configure it
wizard.destination.next-configure.html: Hands the backend and the name to the configure step, which collects the settings, proves them and performs the one create. Nothing has been written yet.

wizard.preflight.check.label: Check result
wizard.preflight.check.html: One step of the connection test: what was tried, how it came out, the engine's category for a failure and its own sentence about it. A step after a failing one was never attempted rather than proven, which is why it is marked apart from a pass.

wizard.s3.step.label: Step position
wizard.s3.step.html: Which of the four steps is showing. Nothing is saved before the last one, so leaving earlier costs only the answers typed.

wizard.s3.provider-preset.label: Provider preset
wizard.s3.provider-preset.html: Fills the endpoint field with this provider's own address and changes nothing else. The value is handed to the transport unexamined, so it can still be edited.

wizard.s3.cancel.label: Cancel
wizard.s3.cancel.html: Closes these steps without creating or changing a destination.

wizard.s3.next-credentials.label: Next: credentials
wizard.s3.next-credentials.html: Moves to how the key is supplied. Unavailable until the destination id and the bucket are both filled in.

wizard.s3.back.label: Back
wizard.s3.back.html: Returns to the previous step with what was typed kept. Nothing is written until the save on the last step.

wizard.s3.next-from-credentials.label: Next
wizard.s3.next-from-credentials.html: Exchanges a pasted key for a stored reference, if one was pasted, and moves on: to the connection test, or straight to the save when this edit keeps the credential already configured.

wizard.s3.retest.label: Test connection again
wizard.s3.retest.html: Writes a real object to the bucket, reads it back and deletes it, using the values on the form. Nothing is saved by checking.

wizard.s3.next-save.label: Next: save
wizard.s3.next-save.html: Moves to the final step. Available only while the check on this screen has passed.

wizard.s3.yaml-preview.label: What gets written
wizard.s3.yaml-preview.html: The configuration this save adds to the deployment's configuration file, shown before it is written. No key and no secret appears in it: a configuration file carrying either is a parse error before validation even runs.

wizard.s3.save.label: Save destination
wizard.s3.save.html: Writes this destination in one request. Backups reach it only once a retention tier names it, which is a separate decision.

wizard.set.step.label: Step
wizard.set.step.html: One of the six steps this set is described in. Any of them can be reopened at any time and the answers already given are kept; nothing is written until the save on the review step.

wizard.set.key-stored.label: Stored key
wizard.set.key-stored.html: A key this deployment already holds, with its fingerprint and the sets currently using it. One that needs a passphrase cannot be chosen, because nothing here could resolve it when a backup runs.

wizard.set.key-replace.label: Replace
wizard.set.key-replace.html: Clears the imported key from this screen so another can be pasted. The key already written into the key store stays there.

wizard.set.key-import.label: Import key
wizard.set.key-import.html: Sends the pasted key once to the engine, which stores it and answers with a fingerprint. This screen keeps no copy and cannot show the material again.

wizard.set.trust-host.label: Trust host
wizard.set.trust-host.html: Records the fingerprint above as the host key this set trusts. It settles which machine answers and nothing more: not that the key authenticates, and not that the folder can be read.

wizard.set.refetch-fingerprint.label: Re-fetch fingerprint
wizard.set.refetch-fingerprint.html: Asks the server for the host key it presents now, which is what a rebuilt source needs. It trusts nothing on its own.

wizard.set.review.source.label: Source
wizard.set.review.source.html: The server and the remote folder this set pulls from, as answered in the earlier steps. Changing either means the connection has to be tested again.

wizard.set.review.destination.label: Destination
wizard.set.review.destination.html: The path on this NAS the transferred artifacts are written to. It has to be a mounted, writable location on the machine running the engine.

wizard.set.review.validation.label: Validation
wizard.set.review.validation.html: What proves an artifact good: the transfer check always, the application validator if one was chosen, and how a finished upload is recognised. A validator that rejects an artifact quarantines it and leaves the remote copy in place.

wizard.set.review.host-trust.label: Host trust
wizard.set.review.host-trust.html: Whether this set has a host key on record for its source. A host key that has since changed stops every backup operation for the set until the new fingerprint has been verified independently.

wizard.set.test-connection.label: Test connection
wizard.set.test-connection.html: Resolves the host, connects, checks the host key, authenticates with the selected key and lists the remote folder. It writes nothing on either side, and saving is blocked until it passes.

wizard.set.connection-checks.label: Connection test result
wizard.set.connection-checks.html: Every step of the test with its own verdict, in the order they ran, so a mistyped hostname and an unauthorised key are told apart rather than collapsed into one failure. A step after a failing one was never attempted, which is not a quiet pass.

source.read-only-credentials.label: Source is read-only
source.read-only-credentials.html: The connection test wrote a temporary file under this source's remote path and the account was refused, so these SSH credentials can read this source but not write to it. Backupd therefore cannot delete anything there, and deleting the original after backup cannot be enabled for this set: every remote original is kept. Grant the account write permission on the source and test the connection again to enable source deletion.

wizard.set.remote-handling.label: Remote source handling
wizard.set.remote-handling.html: Whether Backupd deletes the original artifact on the source once its own copy has been transferred, verified, committed and recorded as safe. A source protected from deletion keeps every remote original for good.

wizard.set.go-to-sets.label: Go to backup sets
wizard.set.go-to-sets.html: Leaves these steps for the backup sets list. The set is already created and enabled; only the immediate run failed to start, and a run can be started from that list.

wizard.set.create-anyway.label: Create anyway
wizard.set.create-anyway.html: Creates the set on an id that already has backups recorded against it, which points this set at that history. Those records become this set's, so it is a deliberate choice rather than a retry.

wizard.set.change-id.label: Go back and change it
wizard.set.change-id.html: Dismisses the refusal and leaves the answers as they are so a different name can be given. Nothing was created.

wizard.set.save-enable-run.label: Save, enable and run
wizard.set.save-enable-run.html: Creates the set, leaves it enabled and starts one backup immediately. The schedule is unaffected by that run.

wizard.set.save-enable.label: Save and enable
wizard.set.save-enable.html: Creates the set and leaves it enabled, so it runs at its scheduled times. No backup starts now.

wizard.set.save-disabled.label: Save without enabling
wizard.set.save-disabled.html: Creates the set and leaves it switched off, so nothing runs until somebody enables it. This is how configuration gets written ahead of a source being ready.

wizard.set.save-hint.label: Why saving is blocked
wizard.set.save-hint.html: The one thing still missing before this set can be saved, or the refusal the last attempt met. It names the real reason rather than a general one, so resolving what it says is enough.

wizard.set.back.label: Back
wizard.set.back.html: Moves to the previous step. Answers already given are kept and nothing is written.

wizard.set.step-count.label: Step position
wizard.set.step-count.html: Which of the six steps is showing. The rail at the top of the page moves between them in any order.

wizard.set.continue.label: Continue
wizard.set.continue.html: Moves to the next step. It neither validates nor saves, so a step can be left half-answered and returned to.

wizard.ssh.steps.label: Steps
wizard.ssh.steps.html: The four steps of replacing this set's authentication: choose a key, settle the server's identity, verify, apply. The set goes on using its current method until the last step is applied.

wizard.ssh.close.label: Close
wizard.ssh.close.html: Closes the wizard without changing this set's authentication. A key imported along the way stays in the key store.

wizard.ssh.busy.label: Request in flight
wizard.ssh.busy.html: What this wizard is waiting on. Its controls stay disabled until the answer arrives, so one request cannot overtake another.

wizard.ssh.back.label: Back
wizard.ssh.back.html: Returns to the previous step with the selection and the probe kept. A verification counts only for the key and host key it was run against, so changing either asks for it again.

wizard.ssh.next.label: Next
wizard.ssh.next.html: Moves to the next step, and is unavailable until this one is settled: a key chosen, the server's identity resolved, or the verification passed.

wizard.ssh.apply.label: Apply and close
wizard.ssh.apply.html: Sends one patch replacing this set's key and trusted host key, and nothing else about the set. Available only while the verification has passed for what is selected now.

wizard.ssh.key-stored.label: Key in the store
wizard.ssh.key-stored.html: A key this deployment already holds, named by algorithm, import date and fingerprint, with the sets using it. One that needs a passphrase cannot be chosen, because nothing could resolve it when a backup runs.

wizard.ssh.key-candidate.label: Key found on this machine
wizard.ssh.key-candidate.html: A private key the engine can read at this path. Choosing it imports a copy into the key store and leaves the original file alone, so the material never crosses the network.

wizard.ssh.import-key.label: Import and use this key
wizard.ssh.import-key.html: Sends the pasted key once, validates it and writes it into the key store with owner-only permissions. It is never displayed again, and this screen drops its own copy as the import returns.

wizard.ssh.on-record.label: Host key on record
wizard.ssh.on-record.html: The host key this set trusts for its source at the moment. A deployment that cannot answer what that is has said something different from nothing being trusted.

wizard.ssh.offered.label: Host key offered now
wizard.ssh.offered.html: The host key the server presented to the last probe. One that differs from the record has to be answered before anything can be applied, because a rebuilt server and an intercepted connection look identical from here.

wizard.ssh.probe.label: Ask the server
wizard.ssh.probe.html: Asks the source which host key it offers right now and compares it against the record. It trusts nothing on your behalf.

wizard.ssh.verify.label: Verify
wizard.ssh.verify.html: Runs the selected key against the settled host key and lists the folder this set pulls from. Nothing is written to the server and nothing is persisted here.

wizard.ssh.checks.label: Verification result
wizard.ssh.checks.html: Every step of the run with its verdict and, where one was measured, how long it took. A step that was never attempted says so rather than passing quietly, and a step with no timing was decided by the same call as the one above it.

wizard.ssh.ledger.label: What applying changes
wizard.ssh.ledger.html: The key and host key this set uses now, beside the ones about to replace them. The rest of the set is left untouched by the patch.

wizard.incremental.engine.label: Backup engine
wizard.incremental.engine.html: Artifact pulls finished files a producer leaves for you and keeps each one whole. Incremental snapshots an entire directory tree and stores only content the repository does not already hold. It cannot be changed later: a set that switched would start a second, unrelated history.

wizard.incremental.domain.label: Repository domain
wizard.incremental.domain.html: The encrypted store this set's snapshots live in. Sets that share one share everything about it — its key, its credential, its maintenance, its corruption blast radius — and in exchange store content they have in common only once.

wizard.incremental.consistency.label: Source consistency
wizard.incremental.consistency.html: What you have arranged on the server, which Backupd records rather than detects. It decides whether a file changing mid-run is ordinary or is reported as a broken arrangement. Only frozen image may be called a point in time.

wizard.incremental.verification.label: Verification level
wizard.incremental.verification.html: How far each backup is checked before it counts. A run that proves less than this fails, and only a run that proves it can become the newest known-good restore point.

wizard.incremental.write-probe.label: Write permission
wizard.incremental.write-probe.html: Backupd wrote a scratch file under the source path and deleted it again. It is the only evidence that these credentials could remove a file there, and it is what arms or refuses Delete from source after a verified backup.

sets.source-delete.label: Delete from source
sets.source-delete.html: After a backup is stored and verified, Backupd deletes the file on the server, freeing space there. It never runs on a backup that failed verification.

sets.source-delete.read-only.label: Delete from source unavailable
sets.source-delete.read-only.html: The SSH credentials for this source are read-only: the write test could not create a file on the server, so Backupd cannot delete there either. Grant this account write permission on the source path and re-run the connection test to enable source deletion.

snapshots.reused.label: Reused
snapshots.reused.html: Content this run offered the repository that it already held, so it was not stored again. When the engine cannot account for it the panel says not measured rather than 0 — a zero would read as a backup that deduplicated nothing.

snapshots.achieved-level.label: Verification achieved
snapshots.achieved-level.html: What the check actually performed, which is not always what was asked for. A failed verification proves nothing and carries no level at all.

snapshots.restore.step.label: Step
snapshots.restore.step.html: One of the four questions a restore answers: which snapshot, what inside it, where it goes, and what happens to a file already there. Any of them can be reopened; nothing is submitted until Start restore.

repositories.maintenance-owner.label: Maintenance owner
repositories.maintenance-owner.html: Exactly one instance maintains a repository domain. Another instance reads and writes snapshots here but will not compact or reclaim, so a domain whose owner is switched off stops being maintained until ownership is transferred.
